sample_unit: patients (randomized trial); 64,200 utterances from 16,583 cases in the misalignment analysis

links.outcome: Patient satisfaction, suggestion acceptance, proactive disclosure, and 7-day unplanned recontact in a randomized trial against a text-based LLM
links.effect: In 555 patients, Dolphin was associated with greater satisfaction (98.6% vs. 93.8%), suggestion acceptance (76.1% vs. 58.9%; p < 0.001), proactive disclosure (44.6% vs. 26.5%; p < 0.001), and fewer 7-day unplanned recontacts (12.9% vs. 22.9%; p = 0.002).
links.quote: In 555 patients, Dolphin was associated with greater patient satisfaction (98.6% vs. 93.8%), suggestion acceptance (76.1% vs. 58.9%; p < 0.001), proactive disclosure (44.6% vs. 26.5%; p < 0.001), and fewer 7-day unplanned recontact (12.9% vs. 22.9%; p = 0.002).

links.outcome: Emotion recognition accuracy and semantic consistency of Dolphin versus a matched text-based LLM and human educators
links.effect: Dolphin outperformed the text-based LLM in emotion recognition accuracy (0.886 vs. 0.713) and semantic consistency (84.9% vs. 82.1%; both adjusted p < 0.001), and received higher expert ratings than the LLM and human educators (all p < 0.001).
links.quote: Dolphin outperformed the text-based LLM in emotion recognition accuracy (0.886 vs. 0.713) and semantic consistency (84.9% vs. 82.1%; both adjusted p < 0.001).

unlisted_practices: Adding audio (non-verbal) cues to text-based LLMs to reduce emotional and semantic misalignment in patient education
Branch-level ablation to establish the contribution of each modality

screen.reason: This randomized controlled trial tests a newly developed bimodal (audio/text) LLM against a text-only LLM in real patient education, evaluating model architecture and performance rather than an organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
